title: The residual error of each action cycle is felt in the periaqueductal gray

statements.text: The residual uncertainty from each cycle of behavior, the unmet needs, is evaluated mainly in the periaqueductal gray, the terminus of all affective circuitry, which Merker places in a bottleneck where perception, action and affect meet. Each category of residual error has affective content of its own, and this felt uncertainty sets the neuromodulatory adjustments of sensory and motor priorities, that is, selective arousal.
